claims.text: NbTaTiV is an example of a nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HEA.
High configurational entropy suppresses phase separation in nearly equiatomic HEA nanoparticles.
A high surface-to-volume ratio promotes surface segregation in HEA nanoparticles.
A high surface-to-volume ratio promotes Ostwald ripening in HEA nanoparticles.
Sluggish diffusion kinetically stabilizes the single-phase structure of bulk HEAs.
HEA nanoparticles exhibit accelerated atomic diffusion because surface and near-surface defects provide fast diffusion paths.
Structural evolution of the nanoparticles will be dominated by surface-driven coarsening.
Elements having lower surface energy segregate to the nanoparticle surface to reduce total free energy.
Surface segregation will produce a core-shell morphology or complete phase separation at lower temperatures than bulk instability.
Below a likely critical diameter of 20 nm, the surface-energy term exceeds the stabilizing configurational-entropy term.
Chemical short-range-order clusters form at the nanoparticle surface during structural evolution.
The activation energy for surface diffusion is lower than that for bulk lattice diffusion.
Surface segregation will occur within the first 10–30 minutes of annealing.
The nanoparticle coarsening rate constant will be one to two orders of magnitude higher than bulk diffusion rates.
Phase separation or ordering will occur 100–200°C below the bulk stability limit.
Particles smaller than 10 nm may completely form a core-shell structure or melt or sinter below corresponding bulk temperatures.
Bulk HEAs remain single-phase and stable up to 0.7–0.8 Tm because of high configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion.
For particles larger than 100 nm, bulk properties dominate and the proposed surface-driven intrinsic-instability model fails.
Nearly identical constituent surface energies minimize the driving force for segregation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis concerns five-transition-metal nanoparticles, but NbTaTiV is offered as an example even though it contains only four elements.
